title: Workforce Planning Report: Functional Headcount Forecast, Critical Skills Gap Analysis, and Talent Acquisition Strategy (Internal Mobility vs External Hiring)
subtitle: Workforce Planning — Headcount Forecast, Critical Skill Gaps, Mobility vs Hiring Strategy

document_brief.narrative_theme: This workforce planning report aligns FY2026 growth targets with function-level headcount forecasts, pinpoints the most urgent skill gaps, and defines when to prioritize internal mobility versus external hiring to deliver a cost-effective talent acquisition strategy.

sections.heading: FY2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Drivers
key_facts: Total headcount is projected to increase from 1,240 on 2025-12-31 to 1,360 on 2026-12-31 (+120, +9.7%).
Engineering headcount is forecast to grow from 410 to 470 in FY2026 (+60), and Sales is forecast to grow from 220 to 260 (+40).
Customer Support headcount is forecast to remain flat at 180 in FY2026 due to a planned 15% productivity gain from automation by 2026-09-30.

sections.heading: Critical Skill Gaps, Internal Mobility Feasibility, and Talent Acquisition Plan
key_facts: The FY2026 critical skill gaps are 18 Data Engineers, 12 Cloud Security Engineers, and 25 Enterprise Account Executives.
The internal mobility target is to fill 55% of FY2026 openings via internal moves, up from 41% in FY2025.
The external hiring plan is capped at 65 net-new hires with an average time-to-fill target of 52 days for priority roles starting 2026-01-15.

structure.heading: Critical Skill Gaps, Internal Mobility Feasibility, and Talent Acquisition Plan
text_content: **Critical Skill Gaps, Internal Mobility Feasibility, and Talent Acquisition Plan**

The FY2026 critical skill gaps are concentrated in three areas: 18 Data Engineers, 12 Cloud Security Engineers, and 25 Enterprise Account Executives, creating immediate capacity and delivery risks across data platforms, security operations, and revenue motion. These shortfalls will materially affect roadmap velocity for analytics initiatives, compliance posture for cloud deployments, and quota coverage in enterprise sales territories. Risk mitigation priorities include re-prioritizing high-impact projects, freezing nonessential hiring, and implementing interim contractor support where permissible. The organization should track vacancy days, time-to-productivity, and customer impact metrics monthly to quantify operational exposure and guide resource allocation decisions.

Achieving the internal mobility target requires ramping internal pipelines to fill 55% of FY2026 openings via internal moves, up from 41% in FY2025. Talent Mobility, Learning & Development, and People Operations must operationalize competency maps, career pathways, and a six-month rotation acceleration program focused on Data Engineering and Cloud Security certifications. Metrics will include internal acceptance rate, internal time-to-fill, and retention at 12 months post-move. Incentives such as expedited salary review timelines and relocation support for cross-region moves should be budgeted. Quarterly governance reviews will determine adjustments to the 55% target based on supply-demand signals regularly.

Given internal mobility ambitions, external hiring is intentionally constrained: the external hiring plan is capped at 65 net-new hires to preserve budget and workforce balance. Talent Acquisition will run targeted campaigns with a priority time-to-fill target of 52 days for priority roles starting 2026-01-15, and will prioritize sourcing for remaining gaps in Enterprise Account Executive and Data Engineering roles. The strategy combines direct sourcing, employee referral acceleration, university partnerships, and vetted staffing partners for short-term capacity. Key performance indicators will track cost-per-hire, diversity mix, offer acceptance rate, and onboarding time-to-productivity through FY2026 and quarterly executive reporting.

structure.heading: FY2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Drivers
text_content: **FY2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Drivers**

Total headcount is projected to increase from 1,240 on 2025-12-31 to 1,360 on 2026-12-31 (+120, +9.7%). This growth funds targeted investments in product and go-to-market capacity within the approved operating plan. Hiring will be phased across quarters to align with launch dates and sales cycles while minimizing mix imbalance. Projections assume current attrition and no material M&A; the people plan incorporates monthly tracking of FTE onboarding, offer acceptance, and time-to-fill to ensure targets are met. It includes contingency capacity for seasonal demand and attrition.

Engineering headcount is forecast to grow from 410 to 470 in FY2026 (+60), and Sales is forecast to grow from 220 to 260 (+40). To deliver these increases, the plan emphasizes targeted sourcing channels, converting contractors, and university recruiting for early-career pipelines. Engineering hiring will prioritize cloud, platform, and security skills to support two major product releases; Sales hiring will prioritize enterprise quota-carrying roles with structured onboarding and ramp targets. Cross-functional coordination with People Operations will set monthly requisition targets and throughput goals.

Customer Support headcount is forecast to remain flat at 180 in FY2026 due to a planned 15% productivity gain from automation by 2026-09-30. The automation program, implemented in staged releases through H1 and H2, will increase handle capacity and reduce repeat contacts, enabling maintenance of service levels with steady headcount. Capacity monitoring will track first-contact resolution, average handle time, and backlog; if productivity milestones are delayed, contingency plans include temporary contractor capacity, accelerated hiring, or redeployment of qualified FTEs from lower-priority projects immediately.
